script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

- South Asia: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after Oct 2025 truce.
- Africa: Ukraine: firefighters battle flames and rescue dog from Kyiv ruins.
- Asia: US, Japan rehearse coordinated strikes to challenge PLA control of waters near Taiwan.

A warehouse belonging to KSD publishing house has been damaged due to a Russian attack on Kharkiv on 27 October. Staff are currently assessing the extent of the damage. No employees were injured.

Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen says Finland will continue to support Ukraine and the US-led peace process, accusing Russia of escalating the war and killing civilians.

- Balkan Insight, 12 hours ago: Bosnian Court Verdicts for Wartime Sexual Violence Show Leniency and Disparities.

- Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: EIB to sign framework deal with Canada on critical raw materials.
Deal marks concrete step toward closer ties between the EU and Canada.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after Oct 2025 truce.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, 4 hours ago: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after Oct 2025 truce.
Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October’s US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday. The report ​by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel, examined violations ‌against Palestinian civilians, including children, since the start of the war between Israel and Hamas on October 7, 2023, up to September this year.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, Africanews, 10 hours ago: Sudan drone strikes kill 21, cause mass outages in east.
Sudan’s warring sides have traded drone strikes that killed 21 people in the western Darfur region and left vast swathes of the country’s east without electricity, medics and witnesses said Tuesday. A drone strike on a market in Nyala, the de facto capital of Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in Darfur, killed 21 people and wounded at least 40 others, a medical source and witnesses told AFP. One Nyala resident said a market in the city’s north was struck by a drone on Monday around 8pm (11pm PKT). Another said the market was frequented by young men, particularly RSF fighters.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: Jordan strikes militant groups in Syria after church attack.
The Jordanian military said it had struck “terrorist organisations” in neighbouring Syria on Monday in retaliation for a deadly attack on a church last week, hours after authorities arrested three men they accused of the killings. It said air force jets had “destroyed several terrorist positions” and killed and wounded “numerous members” of groups linked to the perpetrators of the church attack. Syrian authorities reported civilian casualties from the raids, with health officials in Daraa province saying six people, including three children and a woman, were killed.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Watch: Houthis release dramatic drone strike footage from Saudi border regions.
Recent footage unveiled by the Iran-aligned Houthis purports to showcase attacks on Saudi military sites at the borders. The group asserts it has specifically targeted Saudi forces in regions such as Najran, Jizan, and Asir, heightening regional tensions. Statements pointed to strikes on military transport planes and potential assaults on the Saudi defense ministry, intensifying security worries concerning the kingdom's military and crucial energy resources.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: India exported over $850m worth of arms to Europe since start of Ukraine-Russia war.
Amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, India's defence sector is witnessing an impressive surge in ammunition exports to Europe. With military demands on the rise, India has emerged as a key supplier, achieving record export levels. This growth highlights not only India's manufacturing strengths but also its expanding international partnerships. European countries are eager to restock their military supplies, which bodes well for the future of India's defence industry.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: US assigns nuclear submarine to Australia under AUKUS as China expands Pacific footprint.
The Pentagon has announced that the USS Colorado will be the first US Navy submarine in Australia's rotational force. This initiative aims to enhance military presence and deter China's naval influence in the Indo-Pacific region. The USS Colorado is scheduled to join Submarine Rotational Force-West at HMAS Stirling in 2027. The move is part of the trilateral AUKUS security partnership among Australia, the UK, and the US.
